meta.title: Bootstrap Meta Layers: Burn vs Runtime Fetch
meta.subtitle: Addressing meta is burned into the binary at package time; assertion material and live behavior are always fetched and re-verified at runtime. L3/L4 bootstrap a partner device with no configuration; the live signed catalog remains the only runtime authority.

components.label: L1 Publisher keyring
components.sublabel: signature trust root · rotates only via release

components.label: L3 Embedded signed snapshot
components.sublabel: verified envelope fetched at package time · stale after expiry

components.label: L4 Station bootstrap pointer
components.sublabel: origin + name only · trust re-established live

components.label: L5 Device runtime state
components.sublabel: registry · sessions · snapshot cache · never burned

boundaries.label: Burned at compile time — immutable within a release
Factory bootstrap — yields after first accepted refresh
Device-local — never embedded, never mutated by catalog refresh

cards.title: Boot-time use (offline bootstrap)
items: L0/L1/L2 are compiled in: identity, trust root and catalog origins work with no network.
L3 is first visible with embedded freshness before any fetch; it never evaluates directives after a current snapshot exists.
L4 triggers exactly one live discovery when the Station registry is empty; identity trust is established at the Station, never from the burn.

cards.title: Remote distribution use (runtime authority)
items: Background refresh fetches signed envelopes through the L2 origin merge (override, advertised, baked).
An accepted current snapshot supersedes L3; an expired embedded envelope becomes stale and non-actionable.
Catalog refresh never mutates L5: registry, sessions, active Station and actor scope stay device-owned.
